files.why: DTOs are the server shapes; the renamed fields and the deeper line-item nesting change the zod schemas here — this is the layer that 'changes when the API changes'.
toInvoice/toInvoiceDto read the DTO by key and reach dto.lines; they must absorb the renames and the extra nesting level so core/ stays untouched.
MSW seed data is authored in server shape (InvoiceDto) and is zod-parsed on fetch, so it must match the new field names and nested lines or every query throws.
Its inline InvoiceDto fixture hardcodes the old field names and flat lines; update it to the new shape (this is exactly the test that guards the mapping).

uncertain: Whether 'one level deeper' warrants a new named wrapper schema/type in dto.ts (e.g. an InvoiceLinesEnvelope) vs. an inline nested object — either way it stays in dto.ts, but I can't pick the exact shape without the spec.

queries.ts uses z.array(invoiceDtoSchema) for GET /api/invoices; I assume only the line-item payload nests deeper, not the list envelope. If the list response itself gains a wrapper, queries.ts would also need a change.

I deliberately left core/{types,rules,policy}.ts and all of ui/ unchanged on the premise that the mapper insulates them (the architecture's central claim). If a rename is meant to propagate into core vocabulary too, core/types.ts and its dependents would also change.
questions: What is the exact old->new field rename map, and what is the new nesting key/shape for line items (what wraps the current 'lines' array, and what is the wrapper called)?

Do all three endpoints move to the new shape at once — GET /api/invoices, GET /api/invoices/:id, and the PATCH .../void response — or is it a phased/versioned rollout where both shapes must be accepted for a while?
Is this billing-only, or does the scheduling appointment DTO (which shares client_id/appointment_id join keys with billing seed data) also change?
